bugs.expected: Gap in the acceptance set, for B to rule on. R15-P1 (box inside the body, measured at placement with no clip selected) and R15-P2.1 (the box neither moved nor returned) both pass as written, yet the R15-P2.1 flow itself leaves the box outside the body. No criterion covers a body change after placement. Expected: either the box stays inside the body while expanded (re-place when the body shrinks), or B explicitly accepts the overlap.
bugs.actual: The box is outside the body: it overlaps the preview strip's top 12 px (500-512), and elementFromPoint returns the box on 72 sampled preview points. No preview control (wave 541-573, toggle 605-639) is covered, and every list row is still reachable. Placement is computed only on expand and on a window resize, so the same mechanism existed in round 14.

steps: Copy app/ to tmp/studio-real-loop/c-round-15/guard (node_modules junction), and run the 3 focused test files: 116/116

Mutation G6: in ArrangementExportDialog's content keydown handler, change `event.key !== 'Tab'` to `event.key !== 'Tab' && event.key !== 'Enter'`. Enter on the last control (WAV-ის ექსპორტი) would then be preventDefault-ed and move focus to the X instead of exporting.
bugs.expected: R15-U 'only Tab is handled (Enter and Esc are not prevented or stopped)': at least one test fails under a mutation that handles Enter
bugs.actual: 116/116 still pass. The 'only Tab' test presses Enter only on the X (the first control), where the mutated handler is a no-op, so it cannot detect key-filter regressions at the last control. Real-browser Enter on WAV works today (E5), so this is a test-strength gap, not a product defect.
